Excluded because although the study uses VBM (I3), includes a separate FTD patient group (11 FTD patients, likely bvFTD) (I4), and meets minimum sample sizes for patients and controls (I5), it does NOT report a group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting a bvFTD (FTD) patient group against healthy controls (fails I6). The paper’s VBM analyses relate atrophy to Flanker performance across a mixed diagnostic sample rather than presenting a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast, and no explicit whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control contrast are provided (fails I8). No exclusion criteria from E5–E11 apply.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=66) with an age- and gender-matched control group (n=30). The paper performs voxel-based morphometry group-level comparisons of bvFTD subgroups and bvFTD versus controls (whole-brain analyses reported and FWE-corrected results described). The sample is exclusively bvFTD (not pooled with other diagnostic groups) for the bvFTD vs control contrasts. The manuscript contains full methods, results and discussion (full text provided). Therefore it satisfies imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample, minimum sample sizes, group-level bvFTD-vs-control contrasts, sample purity, and reports whole-brain VBM results (coordinates/maps described).

This FDG-PET study meets several inclusion criteria for the review (modality FDG-PET; group-level voxelwise comparisons of patients vs controls; adequate sample sizes) but does not explicitly report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group. The patient group is described as ‘FTLD’ (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification of clinical variant; inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is therefore not satisfied. Because I4 is mandatory, the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I5 (>=6 patients in patient group), I6 (direct group-level patient vs control comparisons), I8 (whole-brain voxelwise SPM analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s disease sample not specified), I7 (sample purity regarding a bvFTD-only group cannot be established). No exclusion criteria from the review list are triggered by the paper as supplied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (12 bvFTD patients) within the sample (I4); the bvFTD group size (n=12) and the control group (n=30) satisfy the minimum sample sizes (I5); the paper reports group-level VBM comparisons of patient groups versus healthy controls (bvFTD vs controls) (I6); the bvFTD group was analyzed separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7); and whole-brain VBM analyses were performed using SPM5 with normalization to standard space (MNI) and reported voxelwise results, fulfilling the coordinates/whole-brain reporting requirement (I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The paper uses VBM and includes a separate behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) and a healthy control group (n=10). The Methods and Results describe group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts of each disease cohort versus controls, including bvFTD versus controls (with VBM outputs reported). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups), and both patient and control groups exceed the minimum sample-size threshold (≥6). Although coordinate tables are not visible in the excerpt, the paper explicitly reports whole-brain VBM comparisons; per screening instructions this is sufficient. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). The paper reports group-level VBM comparisons of the clinical bvFTD subgroup against healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups in that comparison (I7), and whole-brain results are reported from VBM (I8). However, it fails inclusion criterion I5 because the bvFTD patient subgroup is very small (n=3 in the atypical AD subgroup and n=3 in the FTLD subgroup), below the required minimum of 6 patients for the bvFTD group. Therefore the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study uses FDG-PET and reports voxel-wise group comparisons of FTD patients (n=13) vs controls (meets I3, I5, I6, I7, and I8). However, the patient group is described as ‘fronto-temporal dementia (FTD)’ without specifying the behavioral variant (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. Inclusion criterion I4 requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease specifically. Because the paper does not specify that the FTD group is bvFTD (and cannot be assumed), it fails I4 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level imaging contrast directly comparing a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry and task fMRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD n=10 and controls n>=6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no bvFTD vs control group-level imaging comparison reported — authors combined bvFTD with PNFA for the VBM analysis), I7 (sample purity violated — bvFTD pooled with PNFA for the patient imaging group), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic-space coordinates reported for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison because that specific comparison was not performed). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD group (n=27) and age-matched healthy controls (n=14). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses, describes group-level comparisons between each patient group and controls, and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for voxelwise findings (and refers to supplementary tables for patient-vs-control contrasts). The bv-FTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) against controls. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not a case report, not an excluded modality). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion (supplemental tables cited but missing from excerpt do not preclude inclusion per instructions). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality requirement (I3). It uses volumetric structural MRI with whole-brain atrophy (BBSI) and ventricular measures, not VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET. It also does not report voxelwise stereotactic coordinates from a whole-brain comparison (I8 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD participants included as a subgroup), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I6 (group-level bvFTD vs. control comparisons reported), I7 (bvFTD subgroup analyzed separately, not pooled). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is an empirical resting-state fMRI investigation that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and an age-matched healthy control group (n=12). It performs voxel-wise, whole-brain independent component analysis and reports group-level bvFTD versus control contrasts (e.g., bvFTD < controls, bvFTD > controls) with coordinates referenced to MNI space and explicit stereotactic templates. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The full text includes methods, results (with peak coordinates), and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not using disallowed imaging modalities, not a case report).

This FDG-PET study reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM group comparisons between frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients and healthy controls, and describes hypometabolic regions for the FTD subgroup (behavioral/ personality changes consistent with bvFTD). Imaging modality: FDG-PET (I3). Sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (bvFTD phenotype) and semantic dementia (I4); total N=17 patients and N=9 controls, and subgroup FTD was analyzed separately (I5). The paper reports direct group-level contrasts of FTD versus controls (I6) and the FTD group was not pooled with other patient groups in those comparisons (I7). Whole-brain voxel-wise SPM analysis is described (SPM2), and results are reported anatomically (paper likely includes stereotactic coordinates/tables typical for such analyses) (I8). Full text content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Minor uncertainties: exact N for the FTD-only subgroup and explicit coordinate tables are not visible in the excerpt, but per the paper’s described analyses these criteria are reasonably met. No exclusion criteria identified.

This study used FDG-PET with SPM5 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses) and reports group-level comparisons of an FTD patient group (n=7) versus healthy controls (n=18). Patients were diagnosed using established clinical research criteria (reference cited), implying clinically diagnosed FTD (likely behavioral variant under Neary criteria). Whole-brain results were reported after normalization to MNI space and are described in tables/figures. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 threshold for patients and controls. The FTD group was analyzed separately (not pooled), satisfying sample purity. Taken together, the study meets imaging modality (FDG-PET), sample size, direct patient-vs-control contrast, separate FTD group, and whole-brain coordinate reporting criteria. Because the paper does not explicitly state “behavioral variant FTD” in the provided excerpt, there is minor uncertainty whether all FTD cases are bvFTD; however, established clinical criteria were applied (likely Neary criteria), and per review guidance, when a paper reports and compares an FTD group to controls and uses clinical criteria, it should be included. Therefore I include the study with moderate confidence.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET as the imaging modality (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (I4) with a final N=21 and a control group (N=30) satisfying the minimum sample sizes (I5); reports a direct group-level bvFTD versus control voxel-wise comparison (t-tests between bvFTD and controls) (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the manuscript states that coordinates are reported in MNI space and describes whole-brain SPM analyses (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging acquisition and SPM analysis), results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, ROI-only reporting, non-FDG PET tracer, or case-report design). Therefore I include this paper for the review.

This study should be excluded because its imaging approach is structural MRI volumetric analysis using FreeSurfer ROIs rather than an eligible modality (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic coordinates. Specifically, the paper reports ROI-based volumetric correlations and group ROI comparisons (FreeSurfer-defined rDLPFC, rPC, etc.) but no voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET contrast with MNI/Talairach coordinates. Thus it violates inclusion criteria I3 (imaging modality), I6 (direct voxelwise bvFTD vs control contrast in eligible modality), and I8 (whole-brain coordinates). It meets I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD), I5 (sample sizes ≥6 for patient and control groups), and I7 (bvFTD group analyzed separately, not pooled). Exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is therefore triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded for the bvFTD meta-analysis because it does not meet key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (FDG-PET was the imaging modality used), I5 (patient group size: FTLD n=14 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I4 — the patient sample is pathologically confirmed FTLD but is not described or analyzed as a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease group (FTLD subtypes are heterogeneous and not separated); I6 — the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparison of a bvFTD patient group versus a recruited healthy control group (analyses are rater-based region ratings and individual SSP comparisons to a control database, and comparisons are primarily FTLD vs AD); I7 and I8 are therefore not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This VBM study includes patients with FTLD-TDP and reports atrophy patterns by TDP-43 subtype; it uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases among the sample (I4). However, it does NOT report any group-level analysis that directly compares a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls (violates I6). The bvFTD cases are mixed within TDP-43 subtype groups (type 2 and type 3) rather than analyzed as a separate bvFTD group, so the bvFTD-versus-control contrast is not available (violates I7). It is therefore ineligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis requiring bvFTD-only versus control voxelwise comparisons. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (and thus the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates condition I8 is not satisfied for bvFTD specifically). No exclusion criteria from the provided set are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its cohort (I4) and has sufficient sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls) satisfying the >=6 requirement (I5), it does NOT report any group-level analysis that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD patient group against healthy controls. All primary imaging contrasts are by pathological FTLD-TDP subtype versus controls, or between subtypes. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control comparison) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups) are not met; I8 (whole-brain coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast) is also not applicable for a bvFTD contrast. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Hence the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD vs control voxelwise comparisons.

This VBM study includes a distinct bvFTD (frontal variant) subgroup (n=19) and healthy controls (n=22) and used VBM (I3, I4, I5 met). However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting the bvFTD group against healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). Analyses reported are regressions of face-processing scores within the combined FTLD cohort and subgroup-to-subgroup contrasts (tvFTLD vs fvFTLD), not a bvFTD-versus-control group comparison. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no direct bvFTD vs control voxelwise group contrast) and consequently I7 and I8 (these depend on having that comparison). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=21) with both groups >=6 participants (I5); it reports group-level comparisons that directly contrast diagnostic groups including bvFTD versus controls (ANOVA and post-hoc tests showing NC > bvFTD in right parietal lobe) (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM analyses in stereotactic space with voxelwise results (I8). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the review’s core clinical-contrast requirements. Although it uses 18F-FDG PET (I3 satisfied) and has adequate patient group sizes (FTLD N=31, AD N=42; I5 satisfied for patient group), the patient sample is reported as 'FTLD' and not specifically behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Crucially, the paper does not perform a bvFTD versus healthy control group comparison — it compares AD versus FTLD, not patients versus healthy controls (I6 not met). The paper therefore fails the required contrast and sample-purity criteria (I7, I6, I4, I8). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria from the predefined list (E5–E11) apply directly.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level comparisons between a bvFTD patient group and healthy controls. The bvFTD subgroup (N=12) underwent high-resolution MRI and was directly compared with 12 age-matched controls via two-sample t-tests and regression analyses; VBM results and clusters are reported (referenced Table 2 and Figure 1). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (VBM modality; clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; patient N≥6 and control N≥6; direct bvFTD-versus-control group comparison; bvFTD group analyzed separately from other FTD subgroups; whole-brain VBM results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=10) (I4) with an adequate sample size and a healthy control group (n=20) (I5). However, the paper does not report a group-level analysis that directly compares the bvFTD subgroup against healthy controls (the reported patient-vs-control contrast is for the combined FTLD group, and other reported analyses are within-group correlations of personality change and subgroup correlational analyses). Therefore it does not meet I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison), nor I7 (sample purity for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast), nor I8 (reporting stereotactic whole-brain coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Thus the study must be excluded under the review’s criteria because key inclusion criteria I6/I7/I8 are not met.

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level imaging contrast directly comparing the bvFTD patient group to a healthy control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient n=26 and control n=21 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD vs. control group-level imaging comparison reported — VBM results are reported for the combined FTLD cohort rather than bvFTD alone), I7 (sample purity not satisfied for an imaging bvFTD-versus-control contrast because bvFTD patients are pooled with semantic dementia in the reported VBM analyses), I8 (no report of whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control stereotactic coordinates for an imaging contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) were directly triggered by the paper’s content. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (manual hypothalamic tracing) structural MRI analyses and postmortem histology rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses, thus violating the imaging-modality/whole-brain requirement. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size: 18 bvFTD patients and 16 controls), I6 (group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality: VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — study used manual ROI structural MRI and postmortem histology), I8 (reporting whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for bvFTD-versus-control comparison — not applicable as no whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported). Full text appears complete for screening: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study examines frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) as a group (14 FTLD patients) rather than explicitly and specifically recruiting/labeling behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criteria require clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (I4) and a bvFTD-versus-control group-level comparison (I6). Although the paper uses eligible imaging modalities (FDG-PET and MRI) satisfying I3 and has adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (I5), it does not report a bvFTD-specific patient group or a bvFTD vs healthy control contrast, and it is unclear whether the FTLD group is a pure bvFTD sample (violating I7). The paper also does not present stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain comparison (I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are directly met. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting the key diagnostic/sample requirements for this review (I4, I6, I7, I8).

This is a retrospective case series of 8 patients (FBSS) originally evaluated as bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET/SPECT functional imaging performed in 5 patients), I4 (participants had clinical diagnosis of FTD at presentation), I5 (patient group size = 8, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level analysis directly comparing the bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group), I8 (no report of whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison). Exclusion criteria met: E11 (case series without a concurrent healthy control group). Because the study lacks a control group and any direct voxelwise group comparison versus controls (and thus no whole-brain coordinates for such a contrast), it does not satisfy essential inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study uses VBM on MRI and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD subjects (Neary criteria). It reports group-level comparisons of bvFTD pathological subgroups (PiD, CBD, FTLD-TDP type 1) versus a healthy control group and provides peak voxel coordinates (Table 3). However, each bvFTD subgroup compared to controls contains only n=5 patients, which fails the minimum sample-size inclusion criterion (I5: at least 6 patients in the patient group for the bvFTD-versus-control comparison). Although the total bvFTD sample is 15, the paper does not report a combined bvFTD versus control group-level analysis that would meet I5. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are met. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (I4). Sample sizes meet the minimum (FTD n=11 overall; VBM subset FTD n=6, controls n=13) (I5). However, the paper does NOT report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast that directly compares a bvFTD/FTD group against healthy controls. The VBM analyses were covariate-only regressions collapsing across diagnostic groups (patients pooled with AD and SD) rather than an unpooled bvFTD vs control group contrast. Therefore it fails I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) and I7 (bvFTD group unpooled in that comparison). No exclusion criteria from the review list apply. Hence the study must be excluded for not meeting all required inclusion criteria.

Although the study includes a separate bvFTLD group (n=6), uses an SPM5-based voxel-derived volumetry method, and reports group-level comparisons versus healthy controls with adequate control sample (n=30), it reports lobar/ROI volumetric results and ratios rather than whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-based volumetry/VBM-like method), I4 (bvFTLD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and controls ≥6), I6 (group-level bvFTLD vs control comparison), I7 (bvFTLD analyzed separately). Inclusion criterion I8 (reporting whole-brain results with coordinates in stereotactic space) is not met in the provided full text. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (n=14) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 18 controls) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5); reports group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6) with the bvFTD group reported separately (not pooled) (I7); and the analyses were performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with whole-brain results (I8). No exclusion criteria are triggered by the study (e.g., it is not a review, not ROI-only, not exclusively DTI/FC, and not a case report). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an open-label FDG-PET study of memantine in a mixed FTD sample (bvFTD, semantic dementia, PNFA) with n=16 and voxelwise within-subject (pre-post) analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (≥6 patients in the patient sample). Key inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level comparison of bvFTD patients versus a healthy control group), I7 (no bvFTD-versus-control comparison — patient groups are mixed and not compared to controls), and I8 (no whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control stereotactic-coordinate results reported). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails the required patient-versus-control group contrast and related coordinate reporting (I6–I8).

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=21) and an age-/gender-matched healthy control group (n=21), reports voxelwise whole-brain group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) with multiple-comparison correction, and uses voxel-based morphometry in addition to functional connectivity analyses. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper describes whole-brain stereotactic analyses (voxelwise SPM/ICA/seed-based analyses) and reports results in standard space; figures and methods indicate voxelwise coordinates/analyses were performed. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not PET with non-FDG tracer, not case report, etc.). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met, and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5: patient group sizes are below the required minimum (each bvFTD patient group has N=5, <6). The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3), includes bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (I4), reports direct group-level bvFTD-versus-control comparisons (I6), presents bvFTD groups separately (I7), and describes whole-brain VBM results (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a large, pathologically confirmed FTLD series that used voxel-based morphometry and had sufficient sample sizes for several pathological subgroups (e.g. Pick’s disease n=9 with MRI; controls n=35). It therefore meets imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the voxel-based morphometry analyses in the paper are reported by pathological diagnosis (Pick’s, MAPT, TDP-A, TDP-C, etc.) comparing those pathological groups to healthy controls. The paper does not report a group-level VBM (or FDG-PET/fMRI) analysis that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group (the required contrast per I6). Because the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain group comparison is not reported, the study does not meet I6 (and therefore I7 and I8 are not satisfied for a bvFTD contrast). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (sample includes bvFTD and Pick’s disease patients), I5 (patient subgroup sizes ≥6 for some comparisons and control group ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD vs. control group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD-versus-control purity not demonstrated), I8 (no clear report of whole-brain coordinates for a bvFTD vs control contrast). Therefore excluded.

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses contrasting a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=14) against healthy controls (40) in MNI space, with peak clusters summarized and imaging methods described. Imaging modality = VBM (I3). Sample includes bvFTD patients (I4) and satisfies minimum group sizes for patients and controls (I5). The manuscript explicitly reports group-level bvFTD versus control contrasts (I6), treats bvFTD separately from other patient groups (I7), and reports whole-brain stereotactic-space results (or describes them and tables/peaks) (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging methods, and figures/tables referenced).

The study is excluded because it does not report any group-level comparison between bvFTD patients and a healthy control group (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The paper performs voxel-wise regressions relating occupational attributes to rCMRglc within a bvFTD patient sample (31 patients), reporting coordinates for those within-group associations, but it does not present a bvFTD versus control contrast or the required whole-brain between-group coordinates. It does meet imaging modality (FDG-PET), clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, and minimum patient sample size (I3, I4, I5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but the required between-group analyses and corresponding coordinates for a bvFTD vs. control contrast are absent, so it cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside diffusion MRI (satisfies I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (13 bvFTD patients; satisfies I4), has adequate group sizes (13 patients; 25 matched controls for the bvFTD comparison; satisfies I5), and reports group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparisons (VBM and TBSS contrasts bvFTD vs HCbvFTD; satisfies I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). The VBM/TBSS analyses were performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with results reported and supplementary tables/figures noted, satisfying the coordinates requirement (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary materials referenced).

This study should be excluded because it uses cortical thickness (volumetric MRI cortical thickness) as its imaging analysis, and the review exclusion E9 excludes studies that report only cortical thickness methods. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6 for patients and controls), I6 (direct group-level bvFTD vs. control comparison), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain group comparison reported using SPM5). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modalities: VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — the paper uses cortical thickness rather than an accepted modality. Full text appears complete (includes Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED per E9.

This FDG-PET study examines neural correlates of behavioral deficits across a mixed cohort including AD, FTLD (FTD n=3, SD n=6, mixed n=4), MCI and SCI. Inclusion criterion I3 is met (FDG-PET used). However it fails key review requirements for bvFTD-specific group comparisons: there is no group-level analysis that directly compares a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group against a healthy control group (I6 not met). The small number of FTD cases (n=3) also fails the minimum sample size for a bvFTD patient group (I5 not met if bvFTD is the target). The FTLD-versus-SCI comparison pools multiple patient subtypes, violating sample purity (I7). There are no reported whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD contrast (I8 not met). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the necessary inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes adequate overall patient and control group sizes (AD n=19, FTLD n=13, SCI controls n=10), so imaging modality criterion (I3) and minimum sample-size criterion (I5) are met. However, it does not provide a clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group compared directly and exclusively against healthy controls: the FTLD group is pooled (FTD n=3, semantic dementia n=6, mixed n=4) and the reported group-level comparisons are Alzheimer’s disease vs SCI and FTLD vs SCI. There is no bvFTD-only versus control contrast, nor are coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison. Therefore criteria I4 (bvFTD sample), I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group-level contrast), I7 (bvFTD group purity), and I8 (coordinates for bvFTD-vs-control) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T MRI and performed direct voxel-wise group comparisons between 11 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 11 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for both groups. The paper reports whole-brain VBM results (bvFTD vs controls) and describes the statistical thresholds and FDR correction; the bvFTD group was analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes recruited controls, imaging modality VBM).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its cohort; it also reports group-wise VBM comparisons with healthy controls (patient group n=11, controls n=15). However, the imaging group-level analyses compare a genetic subgroup (C9ORF72 mutation carriers) composed of mixed clinical syndromes (bvFTD, FTD–MND, PPA, etc.) against controls. The paper does not report a group-level VBM (or other included modality) comparison of a bvFTD-only patient group versus healthy controls, and the bvFTD cases are pooled with other FTLD subtypes for imaging analyses. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring a direct bvFTD vs control group comparison and that the bvFTD group not be pooled with other patient groups. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare multiple bvFTD patient groups (C9ORF72, MAPT, GRN, and sporadic bvFTD) against a recruited healthy control group (n=40). Patient groups each contained >6 participants (C9ORF72 n=19; MAPT n=25; GRN n=12; sporadic n=20). The paper reports group-level bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise comparisons and whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected maps and direct between-group contrasts). Groups were not pooled with other dementia syndromes (bvFTD groups analyzed separately). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC-only, PET non-FDG) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 and should be included.

Full text provided is only the abstract, so essential details cannot be verified. The study does use Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and includes a bvFTD sample (satisfying I3 and I4). However, the abstract does not report the number of patients or controls (I5 not verifiable), does not clearly state that a group-level imaging comparison of bvFTD versus healthy controls was performed (I6 not verifiable), does not confirm that the bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast (I7 not verifiable), and does not provide whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (I8 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met based on the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete here, I cannot confirm critical inclusion criteria; therefore I exclude provisionally and flag the record as fulltext_incomplete for retrieval and re-assessment when the full article is available.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3 satisfied) and includes clinically-diagnosed FTD syndromes including behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) and Pick’s disease cases (I4 satisfied). However, it does NOT meet key review inclusion criteria: (I5) the paper does not report the number of bvFTD participants separately or demonstrate at least 6 bvFTD patients in a bvFTD group (patient-group count for bvFTD is not provided); (I6) there is no reported group-level whole-brain comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group — VBM results focus on correlations across FTLD subjects and specific contrasts for PSP or other pathologic subgroups vs controls, not a bvFTD vs control contrast; (I7) bvFTD is not analyzed as a standalone, pure bvFTD-versus-control group in the reported comparisons; (I8) no whole-brain coordinate table is reported for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast. Therefore the study is excluded for not satisfying I5–I8. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with a large overall sample (I5). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain contrast that directly compares the bvFTD patient group against a recruited healthy control group (I6 not met). The presented analyses focus on genotype effects across all subjects and pooled patient groups, and although diagnosis was included as a factor, no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast or coordinates for such a comparison are reported (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review apply. Because criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) is essential and not satisfied, the paper must be excluded.

Excluded because imaging and analysis do not meet the review’s neuroimaging criteria. This study used Freesurfer regional volumetry (ROI-based cortical/subcortical volumes) and correlation/regression analyses rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons. Specifically: Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients are included, n=32), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I7 (bvFTD reported as a separate diagnostic group, not pooled). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no reported group-level whole-brain bvFTD vs control contrast), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate results for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison). Full text appears complete. Because a required inclusion criterion (appropriate imaging modality and bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast with coordinates) is not satisfied, the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on structural MRI and reports whole-brain group comparisons. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=49; MRI subset n=37) and a healthy senior control group (n=30). The authors performed direct group-level two-sample t-tests comparing bvFTD versus controls (bvFTD < controls) and report whole-brain results and peak voxels (supplementary table referenced). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (VBM modality; clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; sufficient sample sizes; direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison; bvFTD not pooled; whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This PLoS One study (2012) uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports direct group-level contrasts of bvFTD patients versus healthy controls, with methods referencing MNI standard space and whole-brain TFCE/FWE-corrected results. The bvFTD group is a separately reported clinical cohort (n=15) meeting consensus criteria, with an independent healthy control group (n=18). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper reports whole-brain analyses registered to MNI space; although coordinate tables are not visible in the provided excerpt, the methods explicitly state registration to MNI space and whole-brain voxelwise results, and the published paper likely includes coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI-only, not an ineligible PET tracer, not a case report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3–I8) and should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis: (I3) It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality alongside DTI; (I4) it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=13); (I5) group sizes meet minimums (bvFTD n=13, controls n=19); (I6) it reports voxel-wise, group-level comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus healthy controls; (I7) the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other FTLD subtypes) in bvFTD vs control comparisons; (I8) analyses were conducted with whole-brain voxel-wise SPM8 methods in standard stereotactic space (MNI) and report statistical parametric maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present; supplementary data referenced). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain coordinate requirements. It used structural MRI morphometry (automated segmentation and radial-distance shape mapping) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It performed ROI-based putamen shape/volume analyses and did not report whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast (I8 not met); thus it fits exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analysis with no whole-brain results). The study did meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD group), I5 (sample sizes ≥6), I6 (direct group comparison FTD vs controls), and I7 (FTD reported separately, not pooled). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study uses structural MRI volumetrics (BSI, FreeSurfer regional volumes) and nonlinear intra-subject fluid registrations, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET — so it fails inclusion criterion I3 (required imaging modalities). The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (I4), has sufficient sample size (6 patients with longitudinal MRI, 15 controls) (I5), presents group-level patient vs healthy control comparisons of volumetric measures (I6), and the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7). However, it does not report whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic coordinates or a VBM-style whole-brain statistical comparison (I8 not met), and the imaging results are region-of-interest/volume-based with intra-subject voxel maps rather than whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses — meeting exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: task-based fMRI was used (I3); participants were clinically diagnosed bvFTD meeting Neary/revised criteria (I4); sample sizes are adequate (20 bvFTD, 18 controls) (I5); the paper reports direct group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparisons (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and whole-brain results in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are reported (I8, see Table 2). No exclusion criteria are violated. The full text provided contains background, methods, results (including tables/coordinates referenced), and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the clear reporting of whole-brain group contrasts and coordinates, this study should be INCLUDED.

The study used FDG-PET and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (11 bvFTD patients) and healthy controls, meeting I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (bvFTD sample), and I5 (N>=6 for patient and control groups). However, the PET analyses were performed only across patients (bvFTD and AD) using correlations with deficit scores; controls were not included in the voxel-wise PET analyses and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (bvFTD vs control group comparison) is not satisfied, and I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the review appear to be triggered. Because failure to meet I6 is sufficient for exclusion, I recommend excluding this study.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for this review: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=8) alongside SD (I4), has >=6 patients and >=6 controls (FTD subgroups n=8; controls n=16) (I5), reports group-level contrasts directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) (I7), and whole-brain results are reported with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., DLPFC peak x=36,y=42,z=30) (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical resting-state whole-brain fMRI with healthy controls, etc.). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=20) and healthy controls (n=20), but it does NOT report any group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting bvFTD patients versus healthy controls. Imaging analyses are within-patient VBM regressions (correlations of grey matter with task scores) on the patient cohort only (16 scans entered), rather than a bvFTD < control or control > bvFTD contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no direct bvFTD vs control group-level imaging comparison) and consequently I8 (coordinates for such a contrast) is also not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (sample sizes >=6). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a VBM study that includes a separate bvFTD patient group (n=24) and reports whole-brain VBM analyses relating insight scores to grey-matter atrophy. However, the paper does not include or report a recruited healthy control group nor any group-level contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I5 (requires at least 6 participants in the patient group and, if there is a healthy/control group, at least 6 participants in the control group) in practice because no control group is present, and I6 (must report a group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison). Included: I3 (uses VBM) and I4 (bvFTD patients included). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and healthy controls (n=17) and reports voxel-wise MNI coordinates for symptom–imaging correlations; however it does NOT report any group-level VBM contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group against healthy controls. The neuroimaging analyses are regression/correlation analyses of flavour/odour identification performance across the FTLD cohort (with additional models incorporating subgroup membership and a bvFTD-restricted correlation), not a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain comparison. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) and I8 (coordinates reported for that bvFTD-vs-control comparison) are NOT met. Inclusion criteria I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample present), and I5 (sample sizes ≥6) ARE met. No exclusion criteria from the review list apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=20) (I4), and meets the minimum patient group size (>=6) (I5), it does NOT report any group-level comparison directly contrasting bvFTD patients with a healthy control group. The analyses are within-group VBM correlations/regressions between gray-matter volume and SEA sub-scores in bvFTD patients (i.e., no bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast), which fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks the required patient-versus-control group voxelwise comparison.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (and VBM) as imaging modalities (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=30) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5); reports group-level voxel-wise comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus controls (I6) and keeps bvFTD as a separate patient group (not pooled) (I7). The methods describe whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses in MNI space using SPM8/DARTEL and report FWE-corrected voxel/cluster results, indicating whole-brain stereotactic reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical study (not a review), it includes whole-brain analyses (not only ROI or seed-based FC), uses acceptable imaging modalities, and is not a case report. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that the patient group be clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) alone and not pooled with other FTD subtypes. Specifically: (a) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM as an imaging modality), I5 (patient group size ≥6; FTD n=37 and controls present), I6 (reports direct group-level comparisons of FTD vs. controls), and I8 (performs whole-brain VBM/TBM analyses and reports group comparisons). (b) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the paper does not specify that the patient group is bvFTD (the FTD sample includes mixed clinical syndromes and only a few cases are explicitly described as behavioral variant); I7 — sample purity is violated because the authors analysed FTD as a pooled single group comprising multiple clinical syndromes rather than bvFTD alone. (c) No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are directly triggered by this paper. Therefore exclude for failure to meet I4 and I7 (pooled/mixed FTD sample).

This study uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and reports group-level VBM comparisons between a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=15). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled), and the paper reports voxelwise results in MNI space (including a peak coordinate for overlap: x=2, y=26, z=-28). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied: imaging modality (VBM), clinical bvFTD sample, adequate sample sizes, direct bvFTD vs control group-level contrasts, sample purity, and reporting of stereotactic coordinates. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

No exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (sample sizes >=6: bvFTD n=17, controls n=18). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 - the paper does not report a group-level analysis directly comparing a bvFTD-only group against healthy controls (analyses are reported for a combined FTD group comprising bvFTD, svPPA, and nfvPPA); I7 - the bvFTD cases are pooled with other FTD variants in the FTD versus control comparisons (violating sample purity); I8 - there are no whole‑brain stereotactic-space results reported specifically for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing I6, I7, and I8.

The study uses VBM (MRI) and FDG-PET (meets I3) and includes an FTLD patient group (n=11) and controls (n=13) (meets I5 for the pooled FTLD group). However, it does not report analyses specifically on a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group: the FTLD group is pooled (FTD n=4, semantic dementia n=5, mixed n=2), so there is no bvFTD-versus-control contrast and the bvFTD subgroup has only 4 patients (<6). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD sample), I6 (bvFTD vs controls group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups) are not met. I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast) is likewise not satisfied because no bvFTD-specific contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria from the provided list clearly apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) and includes sufficient total FTD patients overall (n≈31, so I5 met). However it does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as a separate patient group — FTD is reported generically without specifying bvFTD (I4 not met). The paper focuses on voxel-based classification and presents discriminative images (e.g. AD vs FTD, AD vs NC) rather than reporting a group-level voxelwise contrast directly comparing a bvFTD patient group versus healthy controls with whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (I6 and I8 not met). Sample purity regarding a bvFTD-only vs control comparison is therefore not satisfied (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Hence the study must be excluded for the review because it fails to meet the bvFTD-specific inclusion criteria and does not provide the required bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise group results.

This paper includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (N=16; MRI available for N=11) and healthy controls (N=16; MRI controls N=14), uses whole-brain voxelwise structural MRI analysis (VBM-style gray matter density using ANTs/SPM8), and reports a two-sample group-level comparison of bvFTD versus healthy seniors with FDR-corrected whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (I3). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (I4), with sufficient group sizes for imaging analyses (neuroimaging n=8 bvFTD, controls n=16; VBM comparison used 8 bvFTD vs 48 controls) satisfying the minimum of 6 participants per group (I5). The paper reports group-level direct comparisons between the bvFTD group and healthy controls for both structural (VBM) and functional (task fMRI) data (bvFTD < controls and reduced activation contrasts) (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately and not pooled with other patient groups (I7). Whole-brain results and region-level findings are reported and referenced in stereotactic space (tables and figures; e.g., Table 2, Table 7, figures) consistent with reporting of coordinates/whole-brain contrasts (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=10) (both ≥6), and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD versus Controls (bvFTD < Controls) with results described in stereotactic space (methods state maximum coordinates provided in MNI). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) and whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only) are presented. The supplied full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4) and a control group (n=19), both exceeding the minimum of 6 participants (I5); reports direct group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD versus healthy controls (bvFTD < Controls and related contrasts) (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); and the paper reports whole-brain analyses in stereotactic space (MNI) with tables/coordinates referenced (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study used FDG-PET and included an FTLD patient group (n=11) but did not include a healthy control group or report any bvFTD-versus-control group comparison. Exclusion E11 applies (clinical series without a control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I5 (patient group size ≥6 for FTLD), I7 (FTLD reported as a separate patient group, not pooled). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (uncertain/absent specification that FTLD group is specifically behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison reported), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the required bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise analysis criterion for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study uses resting-state fMRI (meets imaging modality), includes a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD group (n=18) and a healthy control group (n=50) exceeding the minimum sample sizes, and reports direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD patients and controls across whole-brain network measures (graph-theoretical metrics, nodal analyses, and inter-regional connectivity). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The analyses use AAL whole-brain parcellation (standard stereotactic framework) and report region-level group differences across the whole brain. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all required inclusion criteria: uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain analysis; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and a healthy control group (n=18); reports direct group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls (controls > FTD) with whole-brain VBM results described; bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Although stereotactic coordinates are not visible in the provided excerpt, the paper describes VBM normalization to template space and reports whole-brain cluster results; per screening guidance, this is treated as satisfying the coordinates/whole-brain reporting requirement. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration meets several imaging and sample criteria (uses VBM — I3; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants — I4; bvFTD patient count ≥6 — I5). However, it does not include a healthy control group and does not report any group-level comparison directly contrasting a bvFTD patient group with healthy controls. Instead, the VBM analyses contrast musicophilic versus non-musicophilic subgroups within the FTLD cohort. Therefore it fails the required contrast criterion (I6), the sample-purity contrast requirement (I7) is not satisfied, and there are no reported coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison (I8). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) alongside other FTD subtypes (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=18, controls n=27) (I5); reports group-level, direct bvFTD versus healthy control whole-brain comparisons (bvFTD < controls) (I6); the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) when compared to controls (I7); and whole-brain stereotactic coordinates/locations are reported/overlaid in MNI space (I8). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only analysis, not a review, not PET with non-FDG tracer, not case report, etc.). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the review objective focusing on bvFTD imaging studies using VBM. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a protocol/ongoing cohort study describing methods and aims (LOF study) rather than reporting group-level imaging results comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. It does include FDG-PET as an imaging modality (meets I3), but it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: the sample is defined by late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4 not met); no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparisons are reported (I6 not met); no evidence of a bvFTD-only patient group compared against controls (I7 not met); no reported whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (protocol with introduction, methods, and discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain VBM analyses (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=11) alongside other FTD subtypes and Alzheimer’s disease (I4). Sample sizes meet the minimum requirement: bvFTD n=11 and controls n=15 (I5). The paper describes group-level voxel-wise t-tests comparing patient groups (including behavioural-variant FTD) against healthy controls, i.e. direct bvFTD-versus-control comparisons (I6). The bvFTD group is treated as a separate patient subgroup (not pooled) when reporting atrophy patterns and comparisons with controls (I7). Results are reported in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with clusters overlaid on the MNI brain and peak coordinates provided, satisfying the coordinate reporting requirement (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical whole-brain VBM study with appropriate control group and adequate sample sizes. Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but the core article is present (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) vs healthy controls (n=22) that uses VBM (FSL-VBM) alongside other modalities. The paper reports direct group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons and describes VBM processing aligned to MNI standard space (FLIRT), and reports statistically significant VBM reductions in bvFTD. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other dementia groups (only one bvFTD case with MND is included but the group remains bvFTD). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants (meets I4), and has adequate sample sizes (15 patients, 16 controls; meets I5). However it does NOT provide a group-level voxelwise comparison of bvFTD-only versus healthy controls (I6 not met). The primary imaging contrasts and ROI identification are based on a pooled FTD (bvFTD + semantic dementia) versus controls comparison, so the bvFTD group is pooled with another patient group (I7 not met). Consequently there is no clear report of whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control stereotactic coordinates (I8 not met). Therefore the paper fails required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and an MRI control group (n=12). The methods report voxel-based morphometry preprocessing normalized to MNI space and SPM8 second-level analyses, and the Results describe group-level comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (regional/whole-brain atrophy and tables/figures with peak coordinates referenced). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and matched healthy controls (n=19) using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports group-level voxelwise comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus controls using whole-brain analyses in MNI space (coordinates reported/mentioned) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The bvFTD sample is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This resting-state fMRI study includes bvFTD patients and uses an eligible imaging modality, but it does not report any group-level direct comparison of a bvFTD patient group versus a healthy control group (no bvFTD vs control contrast). The paper reports correlations between Reserve Index and network connectivity within FTD subgroups and comparisons between GRN+ and GRN- patient groups, and analyses of presymptomatic carriers, but no patient-versus-healthy whole-brain contrasts in stereotactic coordinates for bvFTD vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI modality), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (patient group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no direct bvFTD vs healthy control group-level comparison), I7 (sample purity for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast not satisfied/applicable because no such contrast), I8 (no reported whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control stereotactic coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because the imaging modality is diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) rather than one of the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and the analysis is ROI-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise. Exclusion criteria met: E9 (reports only DTI methods) and E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients clinically diagnosed), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the ≥6 requirement: bvFTD n=8, NC n=12), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs. control comparisons), and I7 (bvFTD group is analyzed separately, not pooled with other patient groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET is not used) and I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast; study used ROI DTI analyses). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present). Given the modality and analysis type conflict with the review’s imaging criteria, the study must be excluded.

This study used VBM (T1 MRI) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group with adequate sample size, but it does NOT report any group-level imaging comparison directly contrasting bvFTD patients against a healthy control group. The VBM analyses reported compare AD versus bvFTD (patient vs patient), and the behavioral comparisons that include healthy controls are separate from the VBM imaging sample. Therefore key inclusion criteria for this review are not met: there is no bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise group comparison (I6), and accordingly the associated requirements about group purity (I7) and reporting stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control imaging contrast (I8) cannot be satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample included), I5 (patient and control sample sizes ≥6 in behavioral analyses; bvFTD N=48 for VBM). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered by the paper. Because the imaging comparison of interest (bvFTD vs healthy controls) is absent, the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, and has sufficient sample sizes in the patient (n=15) and control (n=12) groups. However, it does not report a group-level whole-brain comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls. The reported VBM contrasts compare the combined FTD group (bvFTD + SD + PNFA) to controls, and subgroup contrasts (fast vs slow acquisition) include mixed FTD subtypes. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control contrast) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (FSL–VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) with a separate AD group and age-/education-matched healthy controls (n=28). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD ≥6, controls ≥6). The Methods state group comparisons were performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI152) and results/covariate analyses are described for bvFTD vs controls (and separate bvFTD and AD analyses), satisfying the requirement for a direct bvFTD-versus-control group-level analysis. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses FDG-PET and voxel-based whole-brain analyses (meets I3). However, it does not report a patient group explicitly diagnosed as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease; participants are described as a heterogeneous FTLD cohort (fails I4). Consequently, the required bvFTD-versus-control group-level comparison is not present (fails I6). Sample purity is not met because the FTLD group is pooled/heterogeneous rather than a bvFTD-only group (fails I7). Whole-brain voxel-wise results are described, but lack of an explicitly defined bvFTD group means the study does not address the review objective (bvFTD-specific group comparisons). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false). Included criterion met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the list apply specifically (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (two bvFTD groups: C9ORF72 carriers n=8, sporadic bvFTD n=15) and healthy controls (n=15). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses comparing each patient group (C9 and sporadic bvFTD) directly against healthy controls, using MNI stereotaxic space and reporting coordinates (noting coordinates/maximums are described and supplementary tables referenced). bvFTD groups are analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This empirical VBM study directly compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) with healthy controls (n=18) and reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry results after normalization to MNI space. It meets imaging modality (VBM), bvFTD sample, minimum group sizes, and reports group-level bvFTD-versus-control contrasts (controls > FTD and FTD>PSP), with whole-brain analyses and stereotactic normalization described. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Core article content (methods, results, discussion) is present, and no exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only, non-FDG PET, review article, only DTI/FC) are triggered. Hence include.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain voxelwise analysis (Methods: FSL-VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=35) (sample sizes ≥6), reports direct group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls with reported patterns of atrophy, and describes results in MNI standard space (Methods) with at least one stereotactic coordinate reported (e.g. peak voxel X=−36, Y=−24, Z=58). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore I include this paper for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used VBM (voxel-based morphometry) alongside DTI (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=27) (I4) with healthy controls (n=20) and AD patients (I5) satisfying the minimum group sizes, reports group-level contrasts directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is reported separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7), and VBM results are described and reported in standard/MNI space with whole-brain analyses (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply: this is an original empirical study with whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), not a review, not an excluded imaging modality, and not a case report. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level contrasts comparing a separate behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) patient group (n=10) against healthy controls (n=14). Sample sizes meet the >=6 requirement for both patient and control groups. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) and direct bvFTD-versus-control t-tests and accompanying VBM results are presented. The paper provides MNI stereotactic coordinates for atrophy peaks and reports whole-brain VBM results (tables/figures with MNI coordinates). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging tables/coordinates) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3). The sample included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) (I4) and an age-matched healthy control group (n=34), exceeding the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The paper reports patient-control (bvFTD vs. controls) group-level comparisons in the VBM analysis (I6), with patient-control group comparisons tested and described. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other diagnostic groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). The methods describe whole-brain VBM analyses registered to MNI space and report VBM results (including supplementary figures), indicating whole-brain stereotactic reporting consistent with I8. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (15 bvFTD/fd+), and the patient sample size exceeds 6; however it does NOT report any group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison (no recruited control group), nor any whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control contrasts or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (direct patient vs control group comparison) and I8 (whole-brain results in stereotactic space). Because there is no concurrent control group, it also meets exclusion criterion E11 (case series without a control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (contrast requirement not applicable because no comparison), I8. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses VBM (structural MRI) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=28) and healthy controls (n=19), meeting I3, I4, and I5. However, the imaging analyses reported are correlational (voxel-wise regressions of discrepancy scores across a mixed diagnostic sample and polisher/tarnisher subsamples) and do not present a group-level VBM contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). The paper parameterizes diagnosis as covariates and reports regressions across pooled groups rather than a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison with stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group contrast) is not met; consequently I8 (coordinates for such a contrast) is also not satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6, n=11). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality — study uses tensor-based morphometry [TBM], not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as required), I6 (no group-level comparison of bvFTD versus healthy controls; comparison is bvFTD versus early-onset AD), I7 (sample-purity criterion for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison cannot be assessed because no healthy-control contrast is reported), and I8 (cannot confirm reported whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD>control contrast because that contrast was not performed). No exclusion criteria from the provided list directly apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry in a large clinically defined bvFTD sample (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, it does not report any group-level comparison of bvFTD patients versus a healthy control group; all reported VBM analyses are within the patient group (regressions/correlations with reward-seeking scores). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs. control group comparison) is not met, and I8 (coordinates for such a comparison) is consequently not applicable/ not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (meets I3) and includes sufficient group sizes (meets I5).
