However, it does not meet the review’s requirement that the sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) because the patient group is a heterogeneous FTD sample (behavioural, language, corticobasal presentations) and the paper does not present a bvFTD-only group. Consequently, it does not provide a bvFTD-versus-healthy-control group-level comparison (I6) nor a bvFTD-specific, pure patient-vs-control contrast (I7). Although whole-brain VBM was performed (and some coordinates are reported), the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinate-reporting criterion (I8) is not applicable because no bvFTD group was defined for that comparison. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) appear to be triggered. Full text appears complete and sufficient for this determination.

This paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=46), fulfilling imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the imaging results are reported as brain–behaviour (discrepancy score) correlations across a heterogeneous pooled sample and secondary ‘‘shared-effects’’ analyses controlling for group membership. The manuscript does not present a direct, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group against recruited healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls) as required by I6. Because no pure bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise comparison is reported, the paper fails I6 (CONTRAST) and therefore also does not meet I7 (SAMPLE PURITY) and I8 (COORDINATES for a bvFTD vs control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD included), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13) against healthy controls (n=12). It explicitly describes group-level bvFTD vs. control contrasts (e.g., “Compared with controls, bvFTD patients showed decreased gray matter intensity...”) and provides results in MNI stereotaxic space (example coordinate x=14, y=-4, z=-16). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD ≥6; controls ≥6). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 are met and the paper should be INCLUDED for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI (I3); includes a clearly defined behavioral-variant FTD group (bvFTD, n=12) diagnosed clinically (I4); has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=15) exceeding the minimum of 6 (I5); reports group-level cross-sectional voxelwise comparisons of each FTD subtype versus controls (I6); the bvFTD group is analyzed separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the analyses are conducted in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with voxelwise, whole-brain VBM/TBSS results reported (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Confident inclusion based on direct bvFTD vs control whole-brain VBM analyses described in the paper.

This full-text empirical study uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) separate from an ALS group (I4, I7), includes a healthy control group (n=15) and all groups exceed the minimum sample size (I5), and reports group-level, whole-brain comparisons of bvFTD versus controls with Talairach normalization and whole-brain ICA/VBM analyses (I6, I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review and should be included.

The study is an original empirical VBM investigation published in PLoS One that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=23) and healthy controls (n=16), performs whole-brain VBM analyses in MNI space, and reports direct group-level comparisons of bvFTD versus controls with voxelwise results described and displayed. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion (full text present). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects (7 bvFTD cases; meets I4), and has adequate sample sizes (14 patients, 16 controls; meets I5). HOWEVER the paper does not report a group-level comparison of bvFTD alone versus healthy controls. The FTD patient group is pooled (7 bvFTD + 7 avPPA) and all imaging group comparisons are performed on this combined FTD-GRN+ group versus controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E5–E11 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met; included criteria met: I3, I4, I5.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinated-reporting criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the imaging analyses are ROI/volume comparisons from FreeSurfer with no whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, pathology/biomarker-confirmed), I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=25, controls n=25), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs. control comparisons for brain volumes), I7 (bvFTD group is reported separately, not pooled with other patient groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural volumetry and PiB amyloid PET as biomarker — not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because I3 and I8 are not satisfied and E6 applies, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study applies voxel-based morphometry (VBM) within a unified VBM+TBM framework and reports whole-brain SPM comparisons between a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (N=30) and healthy controls (N=14). It therefore meets the modality criterion (I3), includes an FTD patient group (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5), performs direct group-level FTD vs control comparisons (I6), keeps the FTD group separate from other patient groups (I7), and reports whole-brain SPM results (I8). The only ambiguity is that the paper labels the clinical group as “FTD” rather than explicitly stating the behavioral variant (bvFTD). Given the paper’s reported whole-brain VBM analyses of an FTD group with typical bvFTD-like atrophy patterns and the review instruction to include when in doubt, I include this study as relevant to bvFTD-related morphometry.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with group sizes of 14 patients and 14+ controls (I5); reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD groups versus healthy controls for both VBM and functional connectivity (I6); bvFTD groups are analyzed as bvFTD (not pooled with other dementia syndromes) despite some comorbid bvFTD-MND cases (I7); and the study describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses referenced to a stereotactic template and displays voxelwise results (I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are noted but not required. No exclusion criteria are triggered by the provided full text.

This paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and reports whole-brain analyses) and diffusion imaging (I3). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14) (I4, I5). Group-level VBM and DTI contrasts comparing each patient group, including bvFTD, directly against Controls are reported (bvFTD vs Controls) (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). Results are reported in stereotactic space with MNI coordinates given for VBM findings (e.g., x=−14,y=10,z=−22) (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

While this study clearly investigates bvFTD and uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=20) and healthy controls (N=31) meeting the minimum sample-size requirement (I4, I5), it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain imaging contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group against healthy controls (i.e., no bvFTD vs control VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET comparison). Imaging analyses were restricted to within-group correlations in the bvFTD participants only. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) is not met, and consequently I7 and I8 (requirements tied to that between-group contrast) are also not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Recommendation: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I6 (and thus I7, I8).

This study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a bvFTD subgroup (47 bvFTD patients) with adequate sample sizes and healthy controls. However, the imaging analyses reported are within-patient VBM correlations relating atrophy to happiness behavior (patient-only correlational analyses). The paper does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group (e.g., bvFTD < controls). Behavioral group comparisons (FTD vs controls) were reported for facial and physiological measures, but no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain VBM (or fMRI/FDG-PET) contrast with stereotactic coordinates is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs healthy control group-level imaging contrast) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This article uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain VBM analyses. It includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) group (n=18) and a healthy control group (n=18), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper reports direct group-level contrasts comparing controls > bvFTD (VBM contrasts) and presents whole-brain results (figures, tables, and supplemental material referenced, with MNI coordinates mentioned). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) for the bvFTD-versus-control comparison. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because the bvFTD patient group contains only 5 participants, which fails inclusion criterion I5 (minimum 6 patients). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and [18F]FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs control voxel-wise comparisons), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain voxel-wise results with reported local maxima/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are triggered by the content provided. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/references present). Given the definitive sample-size shortfall, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This paper reports a voxel-based morphometry-style whole-brain T1 MRI analysis (GM density) comparing bvFTD patients to healthy seniors, with images warped into MNI space and permutation-based voxelwise group comparisons and regressions. The sample comprises 12 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 14 healthy controls (both >6). The manuscript describes and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (bvFTD < controls) and relates behavioral performance to GM atrophy; analyses are whole-brain in stereotactic space (MNI) and results/figures/tables are reported. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. Full article text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met and the study should be included.

This study is relevant to bvFTD and uses FDG-PET and VBM, includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8 symptomatic) and healthy non-carrier controls (n=8), and reports group-level comparisons (including SC vs NC) for ROI measures. However, the paper did not report whole-brain voxel-wise results (with stereotactic coordinates) specifically for the bvFTD (symptomatic carriers) versus healthy control comparison — the voxel-wise whole-brain analyses were performed for mutation carriers (symptomatic + asymptomatic) versus non-carriers, and the authors state they lacked power to perform voxel-wise comparisons among the three diagnostic groups. Because inclusion criterion I8 (whole-brain coordinates for the bvFTD-versus-control comparison) is not met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects as a sporadic FTD group) and I5 (bvFTD patient group size ≥6; n=15). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality – study uses longitudinal structural MRI with tensor-based morphometry/atrophy measures, not Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison reported), and I8 (no reported whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate results for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because required imaging modality and the critical bvFTD-vs-control contrast are absent, the paper must be excluded.

This task-based fMRI study directly compares clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) to healthy controls (n=11) using group-level two-sample t-tests and reports significant between-group contrasts (text references to tables/SPMs with thresholding and small-volume/whole-brain FWE). Imaging modality (task fMRI), sample diagnosis, sample sizes, direct bvFTD-versus-control group analyses, sample purity (bvFTD group not pooled with other syndromes), and reporting of whole-brain results are all satisfied or clearly described. The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-FDG PET, connectivity-only, case report) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD patients (n=13) versus healthy controls (n=11). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups), sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6), and the VBM methods state results were aligned to MNI space with voxel coordinates provided. The full text includes methods, results and VBM group contrasts versus controls. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a separately reported bvFTD group (n=14) (I4) and healthy controls (n=28) with adequate sample sizes (I5); reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups for that comparison (I7); analyses and figures are presented in MNI space with stereotactic coordinates indicated/overlayed (I8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with a large sample, but it does not report a group-level direct comparison of a bvFTD patient group versus a healthy control group (bvFTD < controls or controls > bvFTD). The imaging analyses focus on voxelwise correlates of "disgusting behaviors" across a heterogeneous patient sample and within-group ROI analyses (bvFTD and svPPA) rather than an independent bvFTD-versus-healthy control whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs healthy control group-level comparison). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample present), I5 (sample sizes >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD vs control group-level comparison). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=12) compared with a control group (n=10); uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality (alongside ASL); reports group-level voxel-wise SPM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls; and indicates whole-brain results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates reported and referenced in supplementary tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including imaging and voxel-wise analysis), Results (group comparisons, correlations, ROC/AUC) and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (FDG tracer used, whole-brain analyses performed, not a review or ROI-only study, not a case report). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (24 bvFTD in behavioural cohort; imaging sample includes 18 bvFTD) (I4); sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=18 for imaging, controls n=15) (I5); it reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons directly contrasting patient groups with healthy controls (bvFTD vs controls) (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); analyses were performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI) and MNI coordinates are reported for imaging results (I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of bvFTD VBM studies.

This study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) (I4) and meets the sample size criterion for the patient group (I5). However, the imaging analyses reported are within-patient VBM correlations of hedonic symptoms across FTLD and separate analyses within AD; there is no reported group-level VBM contrast directly comparing a bvFTD group against a recruited healthy control group (criterion I6 not met). Because no bvFTD-versus-control contrast is reported, sample-purity for such a contrast (I7) and the requirement to report stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control comparison (I8) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this review.

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level VBM comparison of the bvFTD patient group directly versus a healthy control group (required inclusion criterion I6). (a) Exclusion criteria met: None ([]) . (b) Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the ≥6 threshold). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT satisfied: I6 (no reported bvFTD-versus-control group-level contrast; VBM analyses were correlations within patients and within bvFTD subgroup rather than a direct bvFTD vs control comparison), I7 (bvFTD-versus-control contrast not present so purity requirement for that contrast cannot be assessed/satisfied), I8 (no evidence in the paper of reported stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because failing any one required inclusion criterion mandates exclusion, I exclude this paper.

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12 on placebo; 10–12 included in imaging analyses) against healthy controls (n=20), with between-group t-tests and SPM/DARTEL normalization to MNI space and cluster-based FWE thresholding. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The manuscript explicitly describes whole-brain VBM contrasts of bvFTD versus controls, including thresholding and figures of atrophy, indicating reporting in stereotactic space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (VBM), Results (group VBM findings), and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not use any of the eligible imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). It is an MRI structural study using manual ROI tracing and shape analysis of the caudate and putamen (region-of-interest approach) rather than whole-brain voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG analyses; therefore it meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results). The paper does meet several inclusion criteria (I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; I5: adequate sample size, 28 patients and 26 controls; I6: direct bvFTD versus healthy control group comparison; I7: bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups). However I3 (required imaging modality) is not satisfied, and I8 (reporting whole-brain stereotactic coordinates) is not fulfilled. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses and explicitly includes a separately analyzed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=59) and healthy controls (n=61). The manuscript describes voxel-wise group-level contrasts of bvFTD versus controls, and indicates coordinates/local maxima are provided in Supplementary Tables, satisfying reporting in stereotactic space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not using disallowed modalities/tracers, not a case series). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (N=20) (I4) and a healthy control group (N=20), both ≥6 participants (I5); reports a direct group-level VBM comparison between bvFTD and controls (two-sample t-test) (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper reports voxel-wise/regression results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates are given for the IFG peak: −41, 26, 3) (I8). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) and healthy controls (n=37), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI, and reports group-level comparisons and whole-brain analyses. The paper describes generating disease maps for each syndromic group (bvFTD and svPPA) relative to a matched healthy cohort, and reports voxelwise VBM and TBSS results with cluster/peak reporting procedures (SPM8, randomise, cluster extraction), consistent with whole-brain stereotactic reporting. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) and sample sizes exceed the minimum. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Additionally, the imaging results are based on visual ratings and diagnostic accuracy rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported in stereotactic coordinates, so I8 is not met. It meets I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD group >=6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=104; 90 with VBM) with an age-matched control group (n=44). The bvFTD sample is not pooled with other dementia syndromes. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and contrasts. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Confidence is high given clear VBM methodology, group-level patient-versus-control comparisons, and adequate sample/control sizes described in the full text.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4) with n=12 and healthy controls (n=17) satisfying sample size requirements (I5), performs direct group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (I6) with post-hoc contrasts, keeps the bvFTD group separate from other patient groups (I7), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with results referenced in supplement/tables consistent with stereotactic reporting (I8). This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses are reported. This FDG-PET study includes 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets I3, I4, I5, I7 and reports whole-brain SPM analyses suggesting I8). However, the required group-level bvFTD-versus-healthy-control contrast (I6) is not satisfied: the authors compare patients to a normative FDG-PET image database (n=112) rather than to a recruited healthy control group, and the protocol explicitly uses database comparisons for single-subject and group analyses. Per the review’s criteria, comparisons against a normative image database do NOT meet I6, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry and resting-state/task fMRI (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (I4); had adequate sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 19 controls) exceeding the ≥6 threshold (I5); reported direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (VBM and resting-state connectivity two-sample tests) (I6); the bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper reports stereotactic coordinates for key contrasts (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37], IFG [-52,2,14]) and describes whole-brain VBM results (I8). No exclusion criteria were triggered based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study uses whole-brain voxelwise longitudinal MRI methods consistent with VBM-style analyses (I3 satisfied). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes in patient and control groups (I5 satisfied). However, the primary voxelwise comparisons reported combine bvFTD and svPPA into a single FTLD group and compare that combined group to controls. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain contrast of bvFTD patients alone versus healthy controls, so it fails to meet the required direct bvFTD-vs-control contrast (I6 not met) and violates the sample-purity requirement that bvFTD must not be pooled with other patient groups in the bvFTD-vs-control comparison (I7 not met). Because the required bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise comparison is absent, I8 (coordinates for that comparison) is also not met. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=34) and healthy controls (n=30) (I4,I5); reports group-level VBM contrasts directly comparing bvFTD groups to healthy controls (I6); the bvFTD groups are not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM results with supplementary figures/tables (I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria from the review apply. Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD subgroup (n=15) (I4), and has adequate group sizes including controls (n=15) (I5). However it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain comparison that directly contrasts bvFTD patients versus healthy controls (I6 not met). The VBM analyses presented compare a mixed “poor melody” patient subgroup (mixed diagnoses) to controls and perform correlations with all patients merged; bvFTD is not isolated for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast (I7 not met). While the paper reports whole-brain VBM results for other contrasts, there is no bvFTD-specific voxelwise comparison with controls and thus it fails the required contrast and sample-purity criteria. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical longitudinal study using resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3 satisfied). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) alongside AD and healthy control groups (n=22) meeting the sample requirements (I4, I5). The paper reports direct group-level voxel-wise comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (bvFTD < controls reported at follow-up) using whole-brain analyses with nonparametric permutation testing and FWE correction, and refers to coordinate tables/figures (I6, I8). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, non-empirical design, inappropriate imaging modality, or case-series issues). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion; therefore inclusion is appropriate.

This empirical study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=26) and healthy controls (n=22), uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI, and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (whole-brain VBM results with peak coordinates referenced in Supplementary Tables). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled), meeting sample size and contrast requirements. Core article content (methods, results, discussion) is present; supplementary coordinate tables are cited. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG‐PET as an imaging modality alongside ASL‐MRI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=32) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=15), both >6 participants (I5); reports group-level voxel-wise and multivariate (PLS logistic regression and GLM) comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6) with whole-brain normalized images and statistical parametric maps (images were normalized to a template and voxel-wise GLMs thresholded with FDR), which satisfies the requirement for whole-brain results in stereotactic space per review guidance (I8). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) meeting sample purity (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, uses FDG tracer, not case series). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of behavioural-variant FTD that meets all inclusion criteria. Imaging modality: whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used. Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=36) and an FTD-ALS group (n=20) with healthy controls (n=23); all groups exceed the N>=6 requirement. Contrast: group-level comparisons between patient groups and healthy controls are reported, and bvFTD is analyzed as a separate group (bvFTD vs. controls), not pooled with other syndromes. Sample purity: bvFTD is reported separately from FTD-ALS and compared with controls. Coordinates: whole-brain stereotactic results (MNI) are described and reported (supplementary tables e2/e3). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, not a case report). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study should be included for the review.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that includes a separate clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=25). The paper reports group-level whole-brain ICA and dual-regression comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus controls, with results reported in MNI space (methods describe MNI152 registration and results reference MNI coordinates). Sample is not pooled with other patient groups. Imaging modality, sample size, between-group contrast, sample purity, and stereotactic whole-brain reporting meet the review inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=58) with healthy controls, meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise brain–behavior correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample and coatrophy checks; the paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting bvFTD patients versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are met. Full text appears to contain core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) and a healthy control group (n=22) meeting the minimum sample-size threshold, and performed group-level bvFTD versus control whole-brain comparisons (reported as VBM results normalized to MNI space with FWE-corrected statistics). The bvFTD group was analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Whole-brain stereotactic analyses are described in the methods and results (MNI normalization via DARTEL), so criterion for reporting results in stereotactic space is satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses FDG-PET voxel-based analyses (SPM8) normalized to MNI space and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group versus healthy controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (26 bvFTD, 24 controls). The paper describes whole-brain SPM results (clusters, Brodmann areas) and references supplementary tables for detailed maps/coordinates. bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group nor report a direct bvFTD-versus-control group comparison. Instead, the sample consists of presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers compared to healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and resting-state fMRI) and I5 (patient group n=15 and control groups ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs. healthy control contrast reported), I7 (no bvFTD group to assess sample purity), and I8 (no whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control stereotactic coordinates to report). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an empirical VBM study (I3) of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with 52 patients and 52 controls (I5). It reports group-level VBM comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7), and whole-brain analyses were performed with images normalized to MNI space and reported (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusion, so fulltext appears complete.

Although this paper uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a separate bvFTD patient group (n=16) (I4), and has adequate group sizes including controls (I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts the bvFTD group against healthy controls (I6 not met). The VBM analyses described are brain–behavior correlations across the entire sample and co-atrophy checks controlling for group membership, rather than a bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast with stereotactic coordinates (I8 not met). Therefore it fails to meet the required imaging-group comparison inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) appear to be triggered by the provided full text. This study uses FDG-PET (also ASL) and includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD cases with sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=20; controls n=38), so it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4 and I5. However, it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparison of a bvFTD-only patient group versus healthy controls (analyses are based on subject-level Z-maps and visual reader assessments rather than a group contrast), and no stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast are provided. Additionally, the FTD patient group is mixed across subtypes (behavioural variant and semantic dementia at one site), violating the sample-purity requirement. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I8 are not met. No listed exclusion criteria (E5–E11) directly apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical longitudinal voxel-wise analysis of T1-weighted MRI (voxel-based morphometry–style longitudinal change maps) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=44) to a healthy control group (n=97). The study performs group-level voxelwise t-statistic comparisons between bvFTD and controls, treats bvFTD as a separate group (not pooled with other FTLD variants), and reports whole-brain analyses after warping to MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the ≥6 threshold for patients and controls. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This VBM study does not include a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease patient group and therefore does not address the review objective. It reports voxelwise comparisons of pathologically-defined groups (AD, DLB, 3R-tau, 4R-tau, TDP43A, TDP43C) versus controls and between pathology groups, but no bvFTD clinical group is described or directly compared with healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient groups and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison), I7 (no bvFTD group to assess sample purity), I8 (no report of bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates because that comparison was not performed). No exclusion criteria from E5–E11 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, multicenter empirical study using resting-state fMRI and VBM (imaging modalities within scope). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=52) and matched healthy controls (n=60), and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (VBM and whole-brain functional connectivity/graph-theory analyses). The methods state normalization to MNI space and report whole-brain VBM results (with Supporting Information tables), satisfying coordinate reporting expectations per screening guidance. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (imaging subset bvFTD n=14) with a control group (n=27). However, the neuroimaging analyses report correlations between PCA-derived behavioural components and grey/white matter across the transdiagnostic cohort, not a group-level voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls. Therefore it does not satisfy the required contrast criterion for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient and control sample sizes meet minima). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD not analyzed as an isolated group in the required contrast), I8 (no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates reported). This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (FSL-VBM) as an imaging modality (I3); it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=40) with adequate sample sizes (I5); it reports group-level, whole-brain comparisons of single phenotypes versus controls including bvFTD vs controls (I6) and the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) (I7). This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (allowed modality) along with cortical thickness and DTI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=27, controls n=48) (I5); reports group-level direct comparisons of bvFTD versus healthy controls with whole-brain analyses (cortical thickness, TBSS, dual-regression RS-fMRI) (I6); the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) (I7); and the methods describe whole-brain results in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I8). This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=25) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=25) meeting sample size requirements (I5); reports direct voxel-wise group-level comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6) with whole-brain analyses in MNI space and states that maximum voxel coordinates are provided (I8); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and neuroimaging analyses.

This study is excluded because it uses whole-brain cortical thickness analyses derived from structural MRI (vertex-by-vertex cortical thickness), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). This violates exclusion criterion E9 (studies that only report cortical thickness methods are ineligible). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modality). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-wise gray matter (GM) analyses comparing bvFTD (n=32) to healthy controls (n=17) using Randomise in FSL, and summarizes peak atrophy/regressions (table e-1 and figures). Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (VBM-style whole-brain MRI comparison of bvFTD vs controls). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess grey matter (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4); sample sizes meet minimums with bvFTD n=19 and healthy controls n=20 (I5); reports group-level voxel-wise comparisons directly contrasting patient groups with healthy controls (two-sample t-tests) (I6); bvFTD patients are analyzed as a separate group (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM analyses in stereotactic space using SPM/DARTEL consistent with reporting coordinates or maps (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports FDG-PET imaging (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=90 overall; n=12 underwent PET) (I4,I5). The paper describes voxelwise group comparisons of glucose metabolism against a healthy control group and gives subtype-specific hypometabolism results (bvFTD described separately) satisfying the requirement for a direct bvFTD-versus-control group-level contrast (I6) and that the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups for that comparison (I7). Whole-brain voxelwise analysis using SPM8 is described (voxel-by-voxel 2-sample t-test, thresholds reported), indicating whole-brain stereotactic analyses were performed (I8). This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that directly compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=38) to age-matched healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain graph/connectional analyses (network-based statistics). It satisfies imaging modality (I3: rs-fMRI), sample includes bvFTD patients (I4), sample sizes exceed the 6-participant minimum for patient and control groups (I5), and it reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other diagnoses) (I7). The paper describes whole-brain network results and node lists/tables (table e-1) consistent with stereotactic reporting of results (I8). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and healthy controls with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=24 with MRI, controls n=21), it does not report any whole-brain, group-level VBM comparison directly contrasting bvFTD versus healthy controls. The VBM analyses described are multiple regressions performed within the bvFTD patient group correlating atrophy with behavioural valence scores, not a bvFTD < controls (or controls > bvFTD) voxelwise comparison. Therefore Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 participants per group). This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-style whole-brain grey matter W-score maps and frequency maps derived from comparisons to healthy controls, meeting the imaging modality and analysis requirements. This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (N=20; VBM sample N=17) and healthy controls (N=39; VBM controls N=28). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-eligible imaging modality, case report) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Excluded because the imaging analysis does not meet the review’s required modalities and reporting. This study directly addresses bvFTD using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain SPM/DARTEL analyses. The study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes, but it does not provide a group-level comparison of bvFTD-only patients versus healthy controls. This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on genetic FTD mutation carriers versus noncarrier controls and has adequate group sizes, but it does not report analyses that directly compare a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group against healthy controls.
